set.approach: The couloir drops off the north side of Bloody Mountain and is visible from far away along the highway. Access is by Laurel Lakes Road, which leaves Sherwin Creek Road outside Mammoth; it is a rough road meant for 4WD vehicles or ATVs, and its upper end reaches Laurel Lakes beside the foot of the couloir. Without a suitable vehicle the road is walked, which makes for a much longer approach. A broad snow apron rises from the lakes to the start of the couloir, which is split by a central pillar into a broader, less steep left chute and a narrower, steeper right chute.

review.notes: Approach from two independent ski write-ups; no descent for climbers stated.

set.approach: The easiest way in is from Coldwater Creek Campground: take the Emerald Lake trail to Sky Meadows, which leaves a short walk to the foot of Blue Crag. The main wall faces north, stays in shade, and the weather changes quickly at any time of year. This line begins in an angled gully, follows it to a broad snowfield, then takes the right-hand bowl into a left-hand gully that leads up to the summit ridge.

review.notes: Area page for approach; route page for the line. Descent not stated, none written.

set.approach: The easiest way in is from Coldwater Creek Campground: take the Emerald Lake trail to Sky Meadows, which leaves a short walk to the foot of Blue Crag. The main wall faces north, stays in shade, and the weather changes quickly at any time of year. Parties making a longer trip can camp in Gentian Meadows beneath the crag. The route starts up a crack and corner leading to a large block or ramp.
set.descent_text: The route ends on the summit ridge. From there walk down the back side of the peak, circling clockwise with some scrambling here and there, and descend through a couloir.

review.notes: Approach from area page; start, camp and descent from the route page (single source for descent).

set.approach: Start at the Fern Lake trailhead in the June Lake area; the gully can be seen from the trailhead. It is the obvious gully on the lower right (north) side of Carson Peak, formed by a wide ice smear that is visible from the roadside ice and Horsetail Falls while walking in. The approach can carry serious avalanche danger after a large storm, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: After the first stretch of mostly pure water ice, descend third-class ledges on the skier's right side of the flow to return to the base of the climb.

review.notes: Area page: trailhead and avalanche note. Route page: location and descent (single source for descent).

set.approach: Start at the Pine Creek Pass trailhead and follow the trail up toward the pass until the old Brownstone Mine, then leave the trail and head south cross-country up into Tungstar Bowl, where the buttress stands. Allow about three hours for the rough approach, which can involve deep powder and boulders early in the season.

review.notes: Route, leave-trail point and three-hour time agree between area page and AAJ.

set.approach: Start at the Bishop Pass trailhead, but do not follow the trail all the way to Treasure Lakes. Instead cut west under the base of the north ridge and swing around into the bowl below the north face, where the couloir climbs a small glacier on the face.

Hike over Piute Pass from the North Lake trailhead, then turn left shortly after the pass toward Muriel Lake and skirt its east side. The next stretch crosses rugged boulder-strewn shorelines and talus to the Goethe Glacier, from which the north-side couloirs rise.

review.notes: Single source for the north approach; couloir position inferred only from the cirque description, so medium.

set.approach: Follow the Longley Reservoir trail. At the lake cross the dam and climb slabs on its left side to reach the moraine, then follow the left side of the Humphreys Glacier up to the bergschrund below the big forked couloir that cuts the peak's northeast flank.
set.descent_text: From the col at the top of the couloir, a class 4 chute leads up and right to the summit. To get down, either reverse the route or downclimb the East Arete, which suits day trips.

review.notes: Route page; single source for descent.

set.approach: From the North Lake trailhead take the trail to Upper Lamarck Lake, then circle the south shore of that lake clockwise and work up the moraine ridges to reach Wishbone Lake. Climbers have usually camped at Upper Lamarck Lake.
set.descent_text: Descend the southeast slopes of the peak, then follow the use trail and cross-country route back toward Upper Lamarck Lake.

review.notes: Area and route page agree on approach; descent from route page only.

set.approach: From the South Lake parking area take the Bishop Pass trail, fork right onto the Treasure Lakes trail, then leave the trail and climb west over a rock ridge. Beyond it lies the basin below the peak's north side; follow its moraine up to the foot of the face. The couloir is the third of four on the north face, counting Knudtson, Smrz, Harrington and Moynier from the left.

review.notes: Single source; page's own descent is not tied to this couloir, none written.

set.approach: Start at Mosquito Flat and hike the trail toward Mono Pass. From the pass go left (west) up an easy slope to the ridge top and scramble down the far side into the Fourth Recess, the trickiest part of the approach. Descend a broad, low-angle scree chute, turn south and go up the recess, passing Snow Lakes, to reach the glacier under the north face.
set.descent_text: The route ends on the summit plateau, crossed to the summit. The normal way off is the East Couloir route, passing Mills Lake to Ruby Lake where the trail back to the trailhead is picked up. Parties camped in the Fourth Recess can instead go back down the north face.

review.notes: Single route page; area page agrees on access via Mono Pass and the Fourth Recess.

set.approach: Drive Buttermilk Road south from Highway 168 west of Bishop to near its rough upper end, which needs high clearance. A short walk through brush leads to the snow line and the foot of the gully. The central Wahoo Gully runs from the summit area down to this point.

review.notes: Road per both; gully extent per trip report. No climber descent stated.

set.approach: Start at the Pine Creek Pass trailhead and hike up toward the Royce Lakes basin, with a bivouac area near a stream and low whitebark pines below the lakes. From there cross the glacier to the base of the couloir.
set.descent_text: From the summit, class 2-3 ledges and sandy slopes lead down to the Royce-Feather col. The couloir in the col holds neve and ice near its top; slings on a rock horn to the climber's right serve as the first rappel point, and lower down the snow can be downclimbed.

review.notes: Single detailed source (a trip report; rephrased as fact, no counts). Second page only confirms the route name.

set.approach: Start at the Convict Lake Marina parking lot and walk the trail along the lake's right-hand shore, then continue up the canyon. The first pitch comes into view as the canyon opens, and the route starts a short way left of the Mini-Pinner couloir. Most of the climb runs up a couloir, which is avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: The route ends on the south shoulder of Laurel Mountain, well short of the true summit. Hike down the Mini-Pinner couloir, or walk south along the shoulder and enter the canyon at a point where the cliff band is lower. Both descents are in avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast.

set.approach: Start at the Northgate trailhead on the north side of Mount Shasta and follow the trail south to the foot of the ridge.

review.notes: Single page; page's descent note is a crevasse warning, not a descent route.

set.approach: Start at the Brewer Creek trailhead on the mountain's north side and follow the Brewer Creek trail southwest, then west, to the base of the Hotlum Glacier. There is often no water at the trailhead; two-day parties camp by a creek near the glacier terminus and its small pond.

review.notes: Single page; its descent wording is ambiguous, none written.

set.approach: Start at the Pine Creek trailhead and follow the Pine Creek trail to the fork below Pine Creek Pass. Take the left branch uphill to the pass, cross it and drop into French Canyon, then work west along the canyon until the fall shows up on your right, tucked into a big corner that faces right. The approach is long, about nine miles with over 4,000 feet of gain, and in winter the approach and descent take far longer than in summer. The slopes around the fall are avalanche terrain, so check the avalanche forecast.
set.descent_text: The climb ends on the plateau below Mount Merriam. The most direct way down follows the rim of the cliff east, on the climber's right, to a wide gully full of talus that leads back to the base. A faster option is to cross the plateau east-northeast and descend to Pine Creek Pass by a break in the plateau's eastern edge; check the snowfield on the approach to the pass for avalanche hazard first.

review.notes: Approach distance and gain agree in both; route and descent from MP only.
